new.title: Climb the Daniel tower above Nördlingen
new.desc: The 90 m steeple of the late Gothic St.-Georgs-Kirche is the town landmark, reached by about 350 steps. From the top the watch has overlooked the old town and the Ries for centuries.
new.tip: Go on a clear day for a view across the old town to the Ries crater rim. The entry fee is small, so carry cash.

new.title: Walk the complete town wall of Nördlingen
new.desc: The medieval wall, about 2.7 km long, is fully preserved and can be walked in a ring, with five gates and a dozen towers. The round town plan follows the edge of the Ries impact crater.
new.tip: Allow 1 to 1.5 hours; the wall walk is free. Start at the Löpsinger Tor.

new.title: Learn how the Ries crater formed at the Rieskrater-Museum
new.desc: The museum opened in 1990 and explains the meteorite impact about 15 million years ago that created the Nördlinger Ries. Exhibits include a piece of Apollo 16 moon rock.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; a planetarium and guided tours are offered. Check hours on the museum site first.

new.title: Climb the Wallerstein rock for a crater view
new.desc: The Wallersteiner Felsen is a freestanding rock in the Ries with a staircase up to a viewpoint. It is listed among the viewpoints of the Geopark Ries.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; the light is best in the afternoon. Climbing is free.

new.title: Hike the Schäferweg around the Ries from Nördlingen
new.desc: This roughly 20 km circular route starts at the Marienhöhe outdoor pool in Nördlingen and crosses the sheep pastures and hills of the crater landscape.
new.tip: Take water and plan a full day; spring and autumn are the best seasons.

new.title: Tour Burg Harburg above the Wörnitz
new.desc: One of the best preserved medieval castles in Bavaria, it has stood above the Wörnitz since the 12th century and is run by the Fürst zu Oettingen-Wallerstein cultural foundation.
new.tip: Open daily 10:00 to 17:00 from mid March to early November, with hourly tours. Park in the town and walk up.

new.title: Stroll the Reichsstraße in Donauwörth
new.desc: Considered one of the most beautiful street ensembles in southern Germany, it runs up to the Fuggerhaus, now the district office. Gabled houses line the old imperial road.
new.tip: Use the city's historic walking tour leaflet; free to explore.

new.title: Climb the tower of Donauwörth's Liebfrauenmünster
new.desc: The late Gothic brick hall church was built from 1444 to 1467. Its tower room is reached by 218 steps and the bells are among the largest in Swabia.
new.tip: Ask at the tourist office about tower opening times, usually in the warmer months.

new.title: Visit the Baroque Heilig-Kreuz-Münster in Donauwörth
new.desc: The former Benedictine abbey dates back to the 11th century; the church was rebuilt in 1717 to 1720 and the tower in 1747. It remains a pilgrimage church.
new.tip: Free to enter; look for the large Baroque altars and the abbey buildings next door.

new.title: See the dolls of Käthe Kruse in Donauwörth
new.desc: The museum on Pflegstraße shows more than 150 dolls by the doll maker Käthe Kruse, whose workshop was in Donauwörth.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday in summer; hours change in winter, so check the town site.

new.title: Peek into the Rieder Tor and the Haus der Stadtgeschichte
new.desc: The Rieder Tor is the only surviving one of Donauwörth's four large sortie gates and now holds the town history museum on Spitalstraße.
new.tip: Combine with a walk on the Ried island; check museum hours at the tourist office.

new.title: Walk the Ried island and Donauspitz in Donauwörth
new.desc: A historical trail circles the old town island of Ried and ends at the Donauspitz where the Wörnitz meets the Danube.
new.tip: About 1.5 hours at an easy pace; free and mostly flat.

new.title: Explore Schloss Höchstädt
new.desc: The Renaissance castle was built from 1589 to 1603 and holds exhibitions and a café. The Museum Deutscher Fayencen is also in the town.
new.tip: Check exhibition hours before a visit; the café is a good stop after the tour.
new.q: Schloss Höchstädt, Herzogin-Anna-Straße, Höchstädt an der Donau

new.title: Admire the Basilika St. Peter in Dillingen
new.desc: The 17th century basilica is the consecration and burial church of the Augsburg bishops and holds the title Basilica minor from Pope John Paul II. The former prince-bishops' residence stands nearby.
new.tip: Free to enter; the Golden Hall of the former university is open only on guided occasions.
new.q: Basilika St. Peter, Kardinal-von-Waldburg-Straße, Dillingen an der Donau

new.title: Climb the Schimmelturm in Lauingen
new.desc: The 16th century Schimmelturm is part of the medieval town fortifications and gives wide views over the Danube valley.
new.tip: Ask at Lauingen's town office for tower hours.

new.title: Look up at the Bayertor in Landsberg am Lech
new.desc: The late Gothic east gate of 1425 is regarded as one of the finest gate complexes in southern Germany.
new.tip: Free to see from the street; the gate can be climbed on some days for views.

new.title: Visit the Hauptplatz and Rococo Rathaus of Landsberg
new.desc: The triangular main square is framed by the town hall with a Rococo facade by Dominikus Zimmermann, the 13th century Schmalzturm and the Ursuline convent.
new.tip: Free audio guides start and end at the Hauptplatz.

new.title: Watch the Lech spill over the Landsberg weir
new.desc: The broad Lechwehr was built in the 14th century against flooding and is the town signature view, with the old town rising behind it.
new.tip: Best seen from the riverside promenade; free.

new.title: Hike the Lechpark to the Teufelsküche
new.desc: A trail of about 7.5 km follows the Lech from Landsberg past the Teufelsküche and Teufelsschlucht.
new.tip: Wear walking shoes as paths can be wet; free.

new.title: Marvel at the Marienmünster in Dießen
new.desc: The Baroque church of the former Augustinian canons is called one of the most splendid church buildings in the region, alongside the Wieskirche.
new.tip: Free; combine with a walk up the Schatzberg or to the lakefront.

new.title: Hike the Schatzberg loop above Dießen
new.desc: A roughly 3 km loop climbs from Dießen to the Schatzberg, passing a lake viewpoint and the Marienmünster.
new.tip: Easy, about two hours with stops; best on a clear day.

new.title: Take a boat trip on the Ammersee from Dießen
new.desc: Passenger boats cross the Ammersee between Dießen and the other lakeside towns, a popular family excursion.
new.tip: Runs mainly from spring to autumn; check the timetable.
new.q: Schifffahrt Dießen, Seeanlagen, Dießen am Ammersee

new.title: Visit the Carl-Orff-Museum in Dießen
new.desc: The museum in Dießen honours the composer of Carmina Burana, who lived and worked at the Ammersee.
new.tip: Open on selected days; check opening times before a visit.

new.title: Tour Schloss Neuburg and its Flemish Baroque gallery
new.desc: Count Palatine Ottheinrich began the Renaissance palace in 1530; a Baroque east wing followed in 1665 to 1670. The courtyard has sgraffito scenes and the Staatsgalerie shows Flemish Baroque masters including Rubens and van Dyck.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; open 9:00 to 18:00 April to September, 10:00 to 16:00 October to March.
new.q: Schloss Neuburg, Residenzstraße 2, Neuburg an der Donau

new.title: Cycle the Danube cycle path from Neuburg
new.desc: The Donauradweg passes the Renaissance old town of Neuburg on a flat stretch along the river through floodplain forest.
new.tip: Pick up the path at the Donaukai; there are beer gardens along the way.

new.title: See the Lenbachmuseum in Schrobenhausen
new.desc: The museum stands in the birthplace of the painter Franz von Lenbach and shows about 500 items from his estate.
new.tip: Opening hours are limited, especially in winter; check before travelling.

new.title: Learn about asparagus at the Spargelmuseum in Schrobenhausen
new.desc: The European Asparagus Museum occupies a tower of the town wall and tells the story of asparagus, grown here since 1912 in Bavaria's largest asparagus area.
new.tip: Pair it with a walk on the town rampart; in season (April to June) try asparagus at local restaurants.

new.title: Visit the Dachau Concentration Camp Memorial
new.desc: The first Nazi concentration camp opened in 1933 and the site is now a memorial and museum with the preserved camp grounds, crematorium and exhibitions.
new.tip: Open daily 9:00 to 17:00 (closed 24 December); admission is free. Plan about three hours.

new.title: Walk up to Schloss Dachau and its Hofgarten
new.desc: The Renaissance palace of the Wittelsbachs sits on the old town hill; the Hofgarten gives a view over Munich to the Alps.
new.tip: The garden is free; the beer garden is open in summer.

new.title: Enjoy a beer at the Schloss Dachau Biergarten
new.desc: The beer garden beside the palace on the hill is listed among the beer gardens of the Dachau area.
new.tip: Open in the warm months; weekdays are quieter.

new.title: See the Dachau artists' colony at the Gemäldegalerie
new.desc: The permanent exhibition shows the heyday of the artists' colony around 1900, one of Germany's most important along with Worpswede.
new.tip: Combine with the Bezirksmuseum and the old town walk.

new.title: Follow the artists' colony route through Dachau
new.desc: A walk past the houses and studios of the painters who lived in Dachau around 1900, ending on the castle hill.
new.tip: Pick up the leaflet at the tourist office; about 2 hours.

new.title: Visit the Birgittenkloster in Altomünster
new.desc: Founded in 1496, the Birgittine convent has a museum on St.-Birgittenhof that shows the history of the order in Europe.
new.tip: Museum hours are limited (afternoons); check with the municipality.

new.title: Taste the beer of Kapplerbräu in Altomünster
new.desc: A local brewery of the Landkreis Dachau, listed by the district among its brewing houses.
new.tip: Try the Hell with a Bavarian snack; check opening days.

new.title: Sit in the Schlosswirtschaft Mariabrunn near Dachau
new.desc: A country inn at Mariabrunn in Röhrmoos with a beer garden, listed among the beer gardens of the Dachau district.
new.tip: Go on a summer afternoon for Bavarian dishes and Hell beer.

new.title: Tour the Wittelsbacher Schloss in Friedberg
new.desc: The castle in Friedberg now holds the town museum with interactive stations and free audio guides in several languages.
new.tip: The grounds are not publicly accessible; the museum has fixed open days, so check hours.

new.title: Visit the pilgrimage church of Herrgottsruh near Friedberg
new.desc: The Wallfahrtskirche Herrgottsruh is one of the main sights of the Wittelsbacher Land.
new.tip: Free; usually open in the daytime.

new.title: Drink beer at Brauereigasthof Sankt Afra im Felde
new.desc: The Friedberg brewery inn is listed in the Wittelsbacher Land beer garden guide.
new.tip: Order a Helles and a Brotzeit in the beer garden.
new.q: Brauereigasthof Sankt Afra im Felde, Friedberg

new.title: Eat at Gasthaus Bichlmeier in Aichach
new.desc: A traditional inn in Aichach listed among the town's beer gardens.
new.tip: Try a Bavarian roast and a local beer; check weekday hours.

new.title: Visit Kloster Thierhaupten
new.desc: A former Benedictine abbey in the Augsburg district, one of the oldest foundations in Bavaria and attributed to Duke Tassilo III in the 8th century.
new.tip: The church is free; museums and tours have fixed days, so check ahead.

new.title: Visit Museum Oberschönenfeld at the abbey
new.desc: The Swabian folklore and craft museum was set up in 1984 in the stables of Oberschönenfeld abbey in Gessertshausen.
new.tip: Tickets at the entrance; check which weekday it is closed.

new.title: Sit in the Klosterstüble beer garden at Oberschönenfeld
new.desc: A restaurant and beer garden on the abbey grounds, popular with cyclists, next to the museum.
new.tip: Combine with a museum visit; bus 605 runs from Gessertshausen.

new.title: Try Schwarzbräu in Zusmarshausen
new.desc: A well known regional brewery that serves guests in its own beer garden.
new.tip: Order a Helles on the terrace; check seasonal hours.

new.title: Swim at the Rothsee in Zusmarshausen
new.desc: A bathing lake of the municipality of Zusmarshausen.
new.tip: Swimming in summer; check conditions locally.

new.title: Walk the Stauden-Meditations-Weg in Fischach
new.desc: A quiet walk in the Stauden hills near the Staudenlandhalle in Fischach, laid out for rest and reflection.
new.tip: Easy and free; allow an hour.

new.title: Eat at the Gasthof Alter Wirt in Geltendorf
new.desc: A village inn with a beer garden in the Landsberg district.
new.tip: Try a regional dish; check open days.

new.title: Drink at Brauerei Holzhausen near Utting
new.desc: A local brewery at the Ammersee, listed in the district brewery guide.
new.tip: Try the Hell; check opening days.
